title: "2. Primes"
engine: pari-gp

## Finding them

```{gp}
p = nextprime(10^30)
```

`precprime` goes the other way, and the gap between the two neighbours of
$10^{30}$ is `{gp} nextprime(10^30) - precprime(10^30)`:

```{gp}
[precprime(10^30), nextprime(10^30)]
```

## Counting them

`primepi` counts primes up to a bound, exactly — not an estimate:

```{gp}
primepi(10^7)
```

The logarithmic integral is the classical comparison, and it overshoots here
as it does for every bound anyone has checked:

```{gp}
[primepi(10^7), round(real(-eint1(-log(10^7))))]
```

A block of primes comes back as a vector:

```{gp}
primes([10^6, 10^6 + 60])
```

## Testing them

`isprime` proves primality; `ispseudoprime` only makes it very likely. The
2^521 − 1 Mersenne prime is proved in the time it takes to say so:

```{gp}
isprime(2^521 - 1)
```

## Looping over them

`forprime` iterates without building the list first, which is how to count
twin primes below a million without running out of memory:

```{gp}
twins = 0;
forprime (q = 3, 10^6, if (isprime(q + 2), twins++));
twins
```

The largest prime gap below a million, and where it starts:

```{gp}
best = 0; at = 0; last = 2;
forprime (q = 3, 10^6, if (q - last > best, best = q - last; at = last); last = q);
[at, best]
```
